trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after it was deployed, with an error rate of 18%. The same build also failed in staging as v2.3.1-rc. I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped partway with an orchestrator error after updating only us-east, which left the regions on mixed versions. A second attempt finished. All three regions now run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, look into the orchestrator error that stopped the rollout partway, and find out why v2.3.1 went to production when its staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open as INC-0001.

**Rollback**
- The bad release is v2.3.1. It was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Nothing needed change-manager approval, because v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before.
- The first rollback attempt stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error, leaving the regions on different versions. A second attempt finished the job.
- Now all three regions run v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%.

**Incident**
- INC-0001 is a SEV2 for checkout-api and has paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback, the partial-rollout problem and the follow-ups below.
- The request to create the incident timed out. I checked the incident list before trying again and found it had been created, so there's only one and nobody got paged twice.

**Follow-ups in the incident**
- Find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.
- Look into the orchestrator error that stopped the first rollback partway.
- Find out how v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already failed in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
Partial rollback: only us-east moved to v2.3.0. Retrying the rollback, since rolling to the same target version is safe to repeat.
